notebookCorrection.prompt: Precise localized edit. IMAGE 1 is the target illustration; IMAGE 2 is the SCIENTIFIC GEOMETRY REFERENCE that must be followed, not merely style. Change ONLY the graphite sketches on the bottom-left notebook page. Remove old sketches completely. Copy the line topology and arrow directions of BOTH textbook ray diagrams in IMAGE 2 accurately onto the graph-paper notebook as two small faint graphite hand-drawn studies, aligned to the notebook perspective. Upper notebook sketch = LEFT diagram of IMAGE 2, convex mirror divergence. Lower notebook sketch = RIGHT diagram of IMAGE 2, concave mirror convergence. For BOTH sketches put the mirror on LEFT and incoming PARALLEL HORIZONTAL rays on its RIGHT with arrowheads pointing LEFT toward mirror. Convex: mirror bulges toward RIGHT and reflected rays travel back toward RIGHT, fanning outward; reflected arrows point away from mirror. Concave: mirror opens toward RIGHT and reflected rays travel back toward RIGHT, meeting at a single real focus on RIGHT of mirror; reflected arrows point toward focus. Incoming and reflected solid rays must stay on SAME RIGHT SIDE of mirror. Draw three off-axis ray pairs per sketch. No rays pass through mirror. Thin principal axis may be present; hatch the mirror back only on LEFT. Do not copy Chinese captions or letters or add virtual dashed rays; preserve the actual textbook shapes and ray connectivity. Notebook diagram is decorative but must be physically correct. Preserve EVERYTHING outside the graphite sketches including paper squares, pencil, eraser, textures, shadows, apparatus if any, framing and colors. Do not change notebook size or object positions.
